clue.text: Current school principal put pupils into groups

parts.note: the head is the teacher in charge of a school
to stream pupils is to sort them into classes by ability

explanation.surface: A head teacher divides the children into ability sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective for the principal, but it is a noun: a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstream is a stream forming the source of a river, so a flowing current of water.

clue.text: Reheated dish keeps hot

parts.note: to keep something is to have it
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warmed-up meal stays hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped leftover meat cooked again, a classic reheated meal.

clue.text: Help audience assimilate constant loud music

indicators.note: to assimilate is to take something in, so the word for help absorbs the constant

parts.note: aid means help
C is the usual symbol for a constant in physics and maths
the house is the audience in a theatre

explanation.surface: Support from the crowd takes in a steady blast of noisy music.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid house is a style of loud electronic dance music from the late 1980s.

clue.text: Police chief with brilliant plan to case thieves' hideaway?

parts.note: super means excellent or brilliant

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the plan wraps round the hideaway

parts.note: an intent is an aim or plan
a den is a lair or hideout, as a den of thieves

explanation.surface: A senior officer with a clever scheme to stake out a criminal lair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to case' means to enclose, not to inspect a target as burglars do; the question mark flags that a den is only one kind of hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a senior rank in British police forces, above chief inspector.

clue.text: Nothing could be written so completely

definitions.meaning: nothing, as the figure 0 or letter O, is written in a round shape
... can mean thoroughly or completely, as in ... defeated

explanation.definitionFit: Roundly means thoroughly, as in being roundly beaten, and a zero is written as a round figure.

clue.text: Gangster meets men in shady places

parts.note: Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster, giving AL
cove is old British slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A mobster meets some fellows in dark corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoves are recesses set back from a room, places out of the light and so shady.

clue.text: Son joined with Roman low life

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
cum is the Latin, so Roman, word for with

explanation.surface: A boy falls in with an Italian lowlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous word for worthless, despicable people, the dregs of society.

clue.text: Cotton fabric from Karachi notably

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of the words Karachi notably

explanation.surface: Cotton cloth produced in a Pakistani city, especially.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric, used for trousers of the same name.

clue.text: Terrible stigma, brought on charge … before me?

indicators.note: brought on says the first part is placed ahead of the next piece
terrible signals that the word stigma is mangled into a new order

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Someone charged and branded with shame stands in the dock before the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the voice of the answer itself: someone on a charge is brought before the magistrate, who speaks as 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defendants on a charge appear before a magistrate, so the magistrate speaking could say 'before me'.

clue.text: Show surprise, hearing film maker's an East End intellectual

indicators.note: hearing says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.words: film maker's an East End intellectual
parts.note: Satyajit Ray the film maker is an intellectual or highbrow, which a Cockney from the East End of London says without its h

explanation.surface: Expressing astonishment on being told a director is a clever Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Londoners (Cockneys) drop the h, so 'Ray's an 'ighbrow' sounds like the phrase wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an eyebrow is the idiom for showing mild surprise or disapproval.

clue.text: Spare millions kept in large container

indicators.note: kept in says one piece is held inside the container

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for rubbish, a British term
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Excess money stored in a big bin.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be sparing or stingy, so spare as a verb meaning use little of.

clue.text: Not stopping in case gun goes off

indicators.note: goes off suggests the words explode into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Constant precautions in case a firearm discharges.
explanation.definitionFit: Unceasing means continuing without a pause, never stopping.

clue.text: Part of company invested in stocks, creating problems

indicators.note: invested in says the piece is put inside the other, like money placed in stocks

parts.note: shorts are short-dated government stocks in financial jargon
a division is a section of a company

explanation.surface: A section of a business puts money into shares, causing difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' is meant in the arithmetic sense: short divisions are sums worked without writing out the steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Short divisions are simple arithmetic exercises, which school sums call problems.

clue.text: For instance offal is something to arouse repulsion

definitions.meaning: offal is an example of a robust, pungent kind of meat
the phrase also means material too harsh or shocking for some to accept

explanation.definitionFit: Strong meat is literally strongly flavoured meat such as offal and figuratively matter likely to shock or repel.

clue.text: Trip, getting urge to withdraw in competitive event

parts.note: a tour is a trip

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the word for urge runs backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or urge

explanation.surface: A journey prompting a wish to pull out of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney is a tournament, a competition, originally between knights.

clue.text: Photographer at theatre swings camera round

indicators.note: round says the pieces are turned about and read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
to pan is to swing a film camera across a scene

explanation.surface: A cameraman at a playhouse turns his lens about.
explanation.definitionFit: Snapper is informal for a photographer, especially a press one taking snaps.

clue.text: Woman's cold and ailing Paris, needing treatment

indicators.note: needing treatment suggests the letters must be worked on and rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ill means ailing

explanation.surface: A woman with a chill, along with a sick Parisian, needs a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Priscilla is a female first name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Singular state of son seen in distress

indicators.note: in distress signals the words are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: An odd condition of a boy spotted when upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneness is the state of being one, single or unified.

clue.text: Royal lady, a bit of a fruit cake

definitions.meaning: the wife or daughter of a Muslim ruler

definitions.text: a bit of a fruit cake
definitions.meaning: a dried grape, one of the pieces of fruit in a fruit cake

explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a sultan's wife and also a seedless dried grape baked in fruit cake.

clue.text: Revolutionary film showing drug dealer

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary
a film is a thin layer, such as a mist on glass

explanation.surface: A movie about a rebel that depicts a narcotics trafficker.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is a pharmacist, who deals in drugs quite legally.

clue.text: Flirts that in France you'll find in beds

indicators.note: you'll find in says one piece is placed within the beds

parts.note: cots are small beds
que is French for that

explanation.surface: Romantic dalliances in French bedrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: To coquet is to flirt, so coquets means flirts, the verb in third person.

clue.text: Pompous speech disconcerted clique? No danger

indicators.note: disconcerted says the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Bombastic oratory unsettled a faction, which says there is no threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiloquence is pompous, lofty, inflated language.

clue.text: A disciple audibly expressed dismay

indicators.note: audibly expressed says the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: Paul the apostle is a follower of Christ, so a disciple

explanation.surface: A follower voiced his consternation.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror, so to dismay as a verb.

clue.text: Departure of actor, no longer the bee's knees

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
the bee's knees is British slang for the best thing, also called it

explanation.surface: An actor leaves the stage, no longer the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit is the stage direction for an actor leaving, a departure from the scene.

clue.text: Quaker collared by English wise guy in rear section of plane

indicators.note: collared by says the Quaker is held within the wise guy

parts.note: a mage is a wise man or magician
William Penn was a famous Quaker, founder of Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A Quaker arrested by an English smart alec at the back of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The empennage is the tail assembly of an aircraft, its rear section.

clue.text: With race almost finished, vote to take a rest

indicators.note: almost finished says the race word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a relay is a team race
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: The race nearly over, a decision is made to pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' takes the last letter from RELAY, leaving RELA.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to rest and unwind.

clue.text: Ring road charge

definitions.meaning: to ring, as a bell is rung slowly
a fee paid to use a road or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: A bell tolls when it rings, and a toll is a fee charged for using a road.

clue.text: Treaty considered in the bag reportedly after hostilities

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the hostilities

parts.note: war is open hostilities
saw means considered, as in saw fit

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: packed means placed in the bag

explanation.surface: An agreement thought to be secured once the fighting is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Warsaw Pact was the 1955 military treaty between the Soviet Union and its allies.
